name: SNAP Food Assistance
summary: Helps eligible households buy food through state-administered EBT benefits.
next_steps: Review your state's SNAP application page from the official source.
Gather income, household, rent, and utility documents.
Submit the state application and respond quickly to interview or document requests.
notes: Eligibility and asset rules vary by state. This app provides a screening estimate only.

name: Medicaid / CHIP
summary: Health coverage for eligible low-income adults, children, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities.
documents: Immigration or citizenship information when requested
Pregnancy or disability documentation if applicable
next_steps: Check your state's Medicaid or CHIP portal.
Apply through the state agency or the Marketplace.
Upload requested income and household verification documents.
notes: Income rules and covered groups vary by state. This is not an official determination.

name: Housing Choice Voucher / Public Housing
summary: Rental assistance for eligible low-income households, administered locally by public housing agencies.
next_steps: Find your local public housing agency.
Check whether waitlists are open.
Submit the local application and keep contact information current.
notes: Waitlists may be closed or long. Local rules are decisive.

name: LIHEAP Energy Assistance
summary: Helps eligible households with home energy bills, weatherization, or energy crises.
next_steps: Find your state or local LIHEAP office.
Check application season and crisis rules.
Apply with a recent utility bill and income proof.
notes: Funding windows and crisis rules vary by state and season.

name: WIC Nutrition Assistance
summary: Nutrition support for eligible pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding people, infants, and children under age 5.
documents: Pregnancy documentation or child's age records
Health or nutrition screening if requested
next_steps: Contact your local WIC agency.
Schedule a WIC appointment.
Bring identity, income, residency, and pregnancy or child records.
notes: WIC requires categorical eligibility and a nutrition-risk screening.

name: TANF Cash Assistance
summary: Temporary cash assistance and work-support services for eligible families with children.
documents: Proof of children in the household
Work or job-search documentation if requested
next_steps: Visit your state TANF office or benefits portal.
Review family and work requirements.
Submit documents and attend required interviews or appointments.
notes: Rules, time limits, and work requirements vary by state.

name: Unemployment Insurance
summary: Temporary wage replacement for eligible workers who lost work through no fault of their own.
next_steps: Apply through your state unemployment office as soon as possible.
File weekly or biweekly certifications.
Keep records of work search and job contacts if required.
notes: Eligibility depends on state law, wages, separation reason, and ongoing certification.

name: Federal Student Aid / FAFSA
summary: Grants, loans, and work-study aid for eligible students pursuing education or training.
documents: Parent or spouse information if required
next_steps: Create or access your StudentAid.gov account.
Complete the FAFSA for the correct academic year.
Review school aid offers and compare net costs.
notes: Aid depends on program, enrollment, dependency status, and school participation.

name: VA Benefits
summary: Health, education, disability, pension, home loan, and related benefits for eligible service members, veterans, and families.
documents: Income and assets for needs-based programs
next_steps: Create or sign into VA.gov.
Choose the benefit type and review eligibility details.
Submit service records and benefit-specific documents.
notes: Eligibility depends on service history, discharge status, disability, income, and benefit type.

name: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
summary: A refundable tax credit for qualifying workers with low to moderate earned income.
next_steps: Review IRS EITC eligibility rules for the tax year.
Prepare or amend your tax return if eligible.
Keep documentation for earned income and qualifying children.
notes: Credit amount changes by tax year, earned income, filing status, and qualifying children.

name: Child Care Assistance
summary: State and local programs may help eligible families pay for child care while working, studying, or training.
next_steps: Find your state's child care subsidy agency.
Check income, activity, and provider requirements.
Apply and ask about waitlists or priority categories.
notes: Availability, income limits, copays, and waitlists vary by state.

name: Nonprofit Credit Counseling / Debt Help
summary: Certified nonprofit counselors can help review budgets, debts, credit, and repayment options.
next_steps: Contact a reputable nonprofit counseling provider.
Ask about fees before agreeing to any plan.
Avoid organizations promising guaranteed debt elimination or upfront quick fixes.
notes: This is not a government benefit; it is included as a financial-stability resource.

name: Local 211 Human Services Referral
summary: Connects people with local help for food, housing, utilities, transportation, health care, and other essential needs.
documents: Any notices or bills related to the need
next_steps: Call 211 or search the local 211 website.
Explain the urgent need and location.
Ask for program contacts, eligibility details, and application instructions.
notes: Local resource availability changes frequently. Confirm directly with providers.
